title: The First Fire
text:
In the Cherokee story recorded by James Mooney, at first there was no fire and the world was cold. Then the Thunders sent lightning, which set fire to the bottom of a hollow sycamore tree on an island. The animals could see the smoke rising, but the tree stood in water, and nobody knew how to reach it.

The animals held a council. Raven offered to go first, because he was large and strong. He flew over and landed on the tree, but the heat scorched his feathers black, and he came back without fire. Then the little Screech Owl went. As he looked down into the hollow, a blast of hot air nearly burned out his eyes, which are still red. The Hoot Owl and the Horned Owl tried next, and the smoke left white rings around their eyes. The black racer snake swam over and slipped in through a hole at the bottom, but he was scorched black. The great black snake climbed up the outside and fell in, and came out as black as the racer.

At last the Water Spider, small and furry, offered to go. She spun a thread and wove a tiny bowl, fastened it on her back, and ran across the water to the island. She brought back one live coal in her bowl, and that is how the people got fire.
lesson: When the strongest members of a team fail, the solution may come from the smallest one with the right idea. Give everyone a chance to try.
people: Raven, the owls, the snakes, the Water Spider
source: James Mooney, Myths of the Cherokee (1900), The First Fire
